steps.text: The streets of Columbia, as a whole, are generally more spacious and vibrant than those of Siracusa.
But when walking through these streets, one sometimes feels a sense of emptiness, as if one does not belong.

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: Hey you, carwash guy. Heard you're from Siracusa, so I got a question for you.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: I'm here to wash cars, not answer questions.

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: Don't be like that, pal.

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: Relax, we're not here to cause trouble for broke-ass bumpkins like you.

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: Heard a group of your countrymen came into town today, and we just wanna know where they are.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: What business do you have with them?

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: Business? Uhh... catching up on old times?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Old times, huh.

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: Hey, my nonno always used to tell me, 'never forget that you're Siracusan.'

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: You don't look 'Siracusan' to me.

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: Me? Siracusan? Hah!

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: Columbia is the future, pal! It's where the gold certificates are!
The young associates of the Columbian families always heard from their forefathers that they came from Siracusa.
But they've never taken it seriously.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Your roots will always be in Siracusa.

steps.name: Cheerful Columbian
steps.text: It's the crusty old fossils who say stuff like that.

steps.name: Cheerful Columbian
steps.text: Columbia is a land of pioneers! Roots? We don't need roots.

steps.name: Frivolous Columbian
steps.text: That's right, hick. You'd better tell us where your paesani are, if you don't want any 'accidents' happening to your little shop here.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: They're in that bar across the street.

steps.name: Cheerful Columbian
steps.text: You got a good head on your shoulders, pal. Don't see a whole lotta wolf pups out there as bright as you.
To be a pioneer is to invite chaos, and the Columbian families gradually lost the order they should've had amidst this chaos.
But for Siracusa, order stands taller than the law itself.
The carwash worker zones out their noise and commotion, turning and slowly opening a cabinet to produce a tool that he is all too familiar with.
It is heavy and sharp, having been meticulously polished by the carwash worker. The glint reflecting off its blade reminds one of the moonlight in Siracusa.
Then, he slowly walks toward the complacent idiots who have their backs turned to him.
Like a carwash worker who only wants to scrub the floors before opening up shop.
Like a Siracusan.
Texas's eyes snap wide open.
As her vision comes into focus in the darkness, she sees a poster Exusiai put up against her will.
Her hands transmit to her the sensation of the down quilt that Croissant sold to her at a special price when the season changed.
Sora's sleep-assisting CD is still playing.
All of this lets her breathe a sigh of relief.
She understands full well that the dream had never really happened, that the Columbian family never had a chance to pester the Siracusan guest.
As for the carwash worker, she has only met him once.
A dream that has no meaning except to remind her of her Siracusan roots.
Since coming to Lungmen, she hasn't had this dream in a long while.
So why have it now?
She unconsciously wants to see the night outside her window.
The moonlight still shines bright and clean.
Myriad colors still dot Lungmen's nightscape.
But within it all is an existence utterly incompatible with everything around it.
Outside her window, on a rooftop beneath the moon, a wolf is staring directly at her.
If everything surrounding it can be called the creations of civilization, then this wolf is undoubtedly a symbol of the wild wastes.
He does not belong here, and never should have appeared here.
But he still appeared in all his majesty, his figure seeming to tower above everything else around him.

a.text: Come. It is time for you to fulfill your end of the deal.

steps.text: In an instant, Texas understands why she had the dream.
Dreams are not necessarily connected to reality.
But dreams often are omens.
And without a doubt, the dream she had tonight portends—
That her past has come knocking on her door.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Noisy. Excessive. Corrupt.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: How far you've fallen, to become indolent in a place like this.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: But, at least you thought of killing me the moment you saw me.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: That means my trip was still worthwhile.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I can give it a serious try, Zaaro.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: It won't make a difference in the end. Same as seven years ago.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: You should feel grateful, last wolf of Famiglia Texas. Our deal still stands, which means you still have a chance to pay off your debt.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: The wastelands have always played fair.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Stop calling yourself the wastelands.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: It has never cut deals with anyone, 'Signore dei Lupi.'

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Heh. Maybe you've just never gotten close enough.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Stop talking in circles. What do you want me to do?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Follow me back to Siracusa. You are to assist my Fang.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: ...'Fang.'

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Fulfill his request, and consider your debt paid in full.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: At that time, whether you choose to return here or remain there is no longer any of my concern.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: If it ain't Zaaro, Lord of Wolves.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Think you can just show up in my city, take my people, leave like it ain't no thing?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Your brain overgrown with weeds now too? Ah, my bad. Forgot, you ain't even got a brain.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Emperor, my wretched kin.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: How long has it been since we last met? Two hundred years? Three?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: What is this revolting outfit of yours? What are you dressing up as?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: What happened to your sheet music? Or your conductor's baton? Have you finally tired of pretentiously tickling the ivories atop the lofty spires of Leithanien?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Mind your business, Zaaro. As if I'd remember when the last time we met was. Wish there wasn't a last time, hope there won't be a next time, and that I forget about this time.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I don't understand. You can choose to step aside, and then forget all about it.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Did I stutter? Get your sorry ass back to Siracusa, and leave my people outta your shit.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: I don't even get how your brothers and sisters still let you and your pups play your little mob game in Siracusa.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: There are many paths to victory. This was my decision, and it has nothing to do with you.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Y'all had some kinda inside deal there, right?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Like y'all keep to your own turf, keep outta human business.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Take a good look at yourself. You hardly look any different from the humans, and you're telling me to stay out of human affairs?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: What are these toys of yours to the glaciers that have not melted for tens of thousands of years? What are these ridiculous black glasses of yours compared to the lasting darkness of the polar nights?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: And then, there's your so-called 'music.' What need is there for music when you already have the coldest wind?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Throw all of this away, Emperor.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: You are forgetting what you truly are. What 'we' truly are.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: You made up those rules. They ain't for me.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: My life ain't your business, wolfie.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: They came up with something new, I decided I liked it, and I made it mine. Simple as that.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: We've always belonged to the wasteland.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: You showed your ass callin' this land the 'wastes.' Ain't nothin' wasted here to me.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Think you're any different from the humans? Rollin' around the forests of Siracusa didn't get you all hungry for power. You never thought about where all that ambition came from?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Zaaro, you ain't made no progress in millennia, and on top of that, you also picked up the dumbest shit humanity's got on offer.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: (Low snarl)

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Stow your fangs, kid. That's rude.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: There's no point fighting amongst ourselves. Nothing will come of it.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I'm just a messenger, here to claim what's rightfully mine.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: She isn't even qualified to be my pawn yet.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: My people are more than qualified to do anything. Including guttin' you.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Your people?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: She doesn't belong to you, Emperor.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Perhaps, you can ask her opinion.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Seven years ago, when I wanted out of Columbia, Zaaro struck a deal with me.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'd be allowed to go free, and in return, I would do him one favor, in the future.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Without this promise, I wouldn't have made it out of Columbia alive.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Ugh, I know all that. Point is, you gonna leave with him?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Sorry, boss, but I have to honor my word.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: I don't give no shit about deals and words, Zaaro. She's my employee.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Texas, I could, magnanimous man that I am, give you some vacation time and let you sort through all your business. Got nothin' to do with me.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: I mean, Penguin Logistics employees are free, even if they're in Siracusa.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: And you, Zaaro, if you dare get up in her business, I'll show up at your stinkin' lair and rip the tail hairs outta you and every one of your siblings. Make myself a nice broom.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Child of Texas, you may make preparations as you see fit, or say your goodbyes.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: No need. Sorry, boss, but I'm going to need a favor. Tell the girls I'm going to be gone for a while, but I'll be back soon.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: I'll just tell 'em you were cryin' about wanting to head back to Siracusa, and you took a long vacation. I tried to stop you, but you wouldn't take no for an answer.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Then... I'll have to buy them some extra souvenirs, and apologize to them when I get back.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: If you have nothing to say, let's be off.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Fine.
And so, a woman and a wolf walk westward, soon disappearing into the night.
The streetlights flicker on and off.
Volsinii Alleyway

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*... Did I make it?

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Heh, good question.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: When did you—?!

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: You're pretty lucky. Right when took the shot, you bent over to pick up the keys that had fallen under the seat.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: Wh-Who are you people? What did I ever do to you?!

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: 'Did I make it?' Hah! 'Did I make it?'

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Can you make it away from air and water? Can a Siracusan ever get away from the rainy season?

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Who could ever get away from them? Or well, from us?

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: What famiglia do you belong to? I've done everything right. No gambling, no debt. I'm just an ordinary clerk at il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici!

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Ohh, il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici. That's a hot topic around Volsinii these days.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: I... I know the son of Don Bellone!

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: That's enough talking.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: (Now's my chance!)

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Ugh, what a pain in the ass. A little trick won't save you.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: The rain's not letting up, huh.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Want a bite? After all, this is Siracusa, the land of pizza!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I've ordered all the flavors the gourmet guide said were worth ordering!

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: At least one of us is in a good mood.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: You didn't forget why we came here, didja?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Not like worrying about it's gonna do any good.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: We've been asking around. Those guys in the black suits don't ever say anything!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: All I heard is that some family by the name of Bellone recently welcomed a guest. I'm gonna head over and take a look around their place.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: That scene, though, tsk tsk. The fowlbeasts are probably gonna make a detour once they pass by.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Ain't that all the more reason to worry?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Lemme tell you, our girl's from here. With her skills, she won't get into any big trouble.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Plus, we came here with the expectation that we might not see her face-to-face at all. Isn't that right, Sora?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Plays and operas are a very robust scene in Siracusa. Whether you're in a tavern or in a theater, there are always many performances to be found. Siracusans from all walks of life regard opera as a way to unwind.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: They say even the mobsters are no exception.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: So I thought, maybe if I could get into a troupe...

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Gotta hand it to ya, Sora, quick thinkin' there nabbin' this chance through Monster Siren Records.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Coincidentally, my agent just asked if I was interested in going to Siracusa to develop my career, which I turned down because I didn't want to leave Lungmen.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: But even so, ain't Siracusan opera way different from yer usual style?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: It sure is. Both the choreography and the singing will pose major challenges. Plus, we're also talking about a completely different kind of stage.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: But after seeing my performance, the director said he'd be willing to give me a shot.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Aha... If MSR didn't already have a contact ready to go, I would've had to keep waiting.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Are you sure I'm not gonna wake up to find you also disappeared without saying goodbye?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: That's not going to happen!

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: I'm not even brave enough for that.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Speakin' of which, ain't it time for your meetup with the troupe's artistic director?

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: You always had these meetings in some kinda company building or theater before. Crazy he wanted to meet ya in a restaurant like this.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: That's not completely unheard of. Some people prefer to chat in a more natural, everyday setting to get a better feel for the actor.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: An everyday setting, huh.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Poppin' up in Siracusa like this don't feel natural to me in the least. But, all I'n do is hope it goes well.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: When we get back to Lungmen, Texas is payin' for three months of boba tea... No, make that six!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Only six? We've got a chance to make her pay through the nose!

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Wow, the director actually showed.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: H-Help me!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Huh? What's going on?

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Look out!

steps.name: Theater Manager
steps.text: Spectacular! I got some great shots from the rehearsal just now!

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: How was it, Signor Bernardo?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Not bad.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But, not good either.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You're too eager to perform, Lena. It's as if you want ten critics to see twelve different emotions in one of your performances.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But, that's too excessive for my needs.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Just give me one thing, as long as it's yours. Your own grief, your own passion, your own desolation.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's not easy being an actor. You are not a prop on the stage, Lena, and you should not settle for being a prop either.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: S-Si, signor!

steps.name: Theater Manager
steps.text: Director, the guests from Lungmen have arrived.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Very good.

steps.name: Theater Manager
steps.text: Are you sure you need to meet with her personally though? She's just a small-time songstress from Lungmen. I can handle this myself.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Loreno, I know that you, as Lena's uncle, have always sought to impede her potential competitors.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But you could try to hide it a little better.

steps.name: Theater Manager
steps.text: Wait... I'm not trying to hide anything from you at all. It's just that we don't have a particularly deep relationship with Monster Siren Records.

steps.name: Theater Manager
steps.text: Rather, there isn't a single theater troupe in Siracusa who thinks highly of this agency trying so desperately to wriggle into our market.

steps.name: Theater Manager
steps.text: But you went beyond expectations in agreeing to the deal to bring one of their singers over to study at our theater.

steps.name: Theater Manager
steps.text: Both logically and emotionally, this doesn't benefit us at all. And now you're even going to meet her, personally?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's as you said, Loreno. She is just a small-time songstress from Lungmen, with nothing inherently deserving of my attention.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But, as you will soon see, the 'from Lungmen' part holds a special significance.

steps.name: Theater Manager
steps.text: Are you talking about...?

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: (*whispers*)

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Thank you. Tell him, don't go overboard.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's our life, isn't it?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: These guys are actually using explosive bolts?!

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Are you alright, sir?

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: I-I'm fine, for now.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: But you people... you're foreigners, right?

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: You shouldn't have helped me. Getting mixed up with those people is a good way to get killed.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Am I the only one who thinks it's mighty strange that there's a murder in broad daylight and nobody seems to care?!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Grr, these guys are tougher to deal with than the gangsters back in Lungmen.

steps.name: Pensive Hitman
steps.text: You're only making trouble for yourself, straniera.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What a coincidence. The thing I'm second best at is making trouble for myself.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: By the way, the thing I'm best at... is getting rid of those troubles~

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: You're in Siracusa now.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: So what?

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: So that means you have no idea what you're getting yourself into.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Watch out, Exusiai!
Attacking civilians! Which famiglia are you with?
Have you forgotten our ironclad laws?

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Ugh... Talk about bad timing...

steps.name: Pensive Hitman
steps.text: No wonder this little runt kept running toward Lavinia's commute.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Let's get outta here.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Get back here!

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: Judge Lavinia!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I remember you. You're from il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici... What's going on?

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: I-I have no idea! I was just heading to work!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: From the way those guys were dressed up, they should've known the rules. Then, why...

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: I'm just a law-abiding citizen. I've never even gotten mixed up with any of the famiglie! Why, why are they still...

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: Your Honor, don't you think there's been something weird in the air recently?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Are the three of you alright?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I'm fine, but those guys ended up getting away...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Heh, I never expected Siracusa's customs to be so cutthroat.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Foreigners in Siracusa should try to be a bit more careful.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: And who might you be?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I am Lavinia, a judge for this city. What about you?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You can call me Exusiai. And she's Sora.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: And that's Croissant over there.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: First of all, I would like to thank you. Your brave actions saved the life of this innocent civilian.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Need my help chasing those guys down?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Don't bother. They know this city like the backs of their hands, and you won't ever catch them. I'll sort out the rest.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Where are you from?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: We came from Lungmen.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Might as well give you our business card. If'n ya ever need somethin' delivered, you give us a holler~

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Lungmen, Penguin Logistics... You're with a logistics company?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: That's right! No matter what it is, a tiny coin or a big ol' burdenbeast, we can take it wherever you need it to go!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Day or night, rain or shine, the customer's satisfaction is our mission!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Oh, assuming you have the money to pay, that is!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Pfft.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Huh? Is our pitch that funny?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: No, I'm sorry. I've just been a bit on edge lately.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Did you come to Volsinii to expand your business, or just for pleasure?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Either way, you chose an unfortunate time to come.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Well, actually, we came lookin' fer a friend of ours...
Lavinia, we're about to enjoy a grand celebration. What better time could there be to visit?
A new city is about to be born in Volsinii—the greatest event in the history of Siracusa.
Should they be lucky enough, our new friends may get to witness its birth.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Bernardo.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Don't worry. These are my guests.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yours? Or your troupe's?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Which would you prefer?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I hope... it's neither.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: That's too bad then, because the answer is both.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: It's not too late to go back to Lungmen right now, Exusiai.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Whaddya mean?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You always get the wrong idea about me, Lavinia.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I wasn't even the one who invited them here. Signorina Sora chose to come to Volsinii herself. Isn't that right?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Yessir. In fact, I'm grateful to Compagnia dell'alba for being willing to take me.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Alright then. Since you're Signor Bernardo's... guests, you won't have to worry much about your safety, at the very least.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Just, please contact me if you need something, alright? My number's right here.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Can do~

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Now then, I need to ask this gentleman about what happened to him. The rest of you... enjoy your chat.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Bernardo... Bernardo... Oh!!

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Wait, are you the Bernardo, artistic director of Compagnia dell'alba?

spans.text: Bernardo, artistic director of Compagnia dell'alba?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: That I am.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Oh wow... You came all the way out here just for us...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I've always chosen actors myself. After all, you know what they say about wanting a job done well.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: And, who might these two be?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: They're my good friends who came to Siracusa with me.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: We're her bodyguards, too. The name's Croissant.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: And you can just call me Exusiai.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Very interesting names.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Shouldn't we be... moseyin' along?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: There's no need. The famiglia associates don't cause trouble without reason. I'm not sure what kind of mess that clerk got himself into, but Siracusa is not without its own order.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: This ain't your typical 'order' now, is it?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You think so? I got the impression our Sankta friend here would be quite familiar with it.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Nah, even in Laterano, something like that would've been considered straight-up assault!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Hah, the Signora of Siracusa always says she brought 'guns and order' from Laterano, but the reality seems to be a bit different.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The customs here might be a bit too extreme for outsiders. But, if you plan on spending any amount of time here, you'll want to get used to them as quickly as possible.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Setting aside the little intermezzo we just enjoyed, Signorina Sora, is now a good time to discuss your new job?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Oh, of course!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I'm assuming you haven't read the script yet, correct? This is our troupe's latest masterpiece, and your role is found within.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: I-It would be an honor...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: We haven't finalized the title of this production yet, but the name our creative team has chosen for this tragedy in three acts is—

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: 'La Morte di Texas.'

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Wh-What did you just say?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Oh? Seems my play has already captured your attention. Let's take our time and talk.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Oh right, I almost forgot in all the commotion just now.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Benvenuti in Siracusa, mie amiche.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Grr... It just had to be Lavinia again. Rotten luck.

steps.name: Pensive Hitman
steps.text: And there was that Sankta too. Why the hell would a bunch of foreigners just show up in Siracusa, at a time like this? Plus, she had some real skills too...

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Think it might be true that Signora Sicilia's guy might already be in Volsinii?

steps.name: Pensive Hitman
steps.text: Ugh, who cares. Let's head back and then—

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Who's there?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Relax, paesani. I ain't your enemy.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Who do you belong to?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Hmm... If I had to say, I s'pose I'd call myself a Sicilian.

steps.name: Pensive Hitman
steps.text: A Sicilian? Stop joking around. They got rubbed out ages ago.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: I don't have the energy to waste my breath on you, so get outta my way, unless you got a death wish.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: I'm just here to remind you there are people from the court waitin' in ambush over there. Steer clear, if you know what's good for you.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Who the hell are you? I never heard nothin' about nobody coming to talk to us.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Course you didn't. Because I didn't come here to talk to you.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: That brings me to the second thing I'd like to remind you of—

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: The Sicilians may have been erased, but they didn't die out.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: What—

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Urk... Guh...

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: By the way, we came here to silence you.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: You talk too damn much. Hope Lappland's not rubbing off on you.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: That, we can agree on.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Hey, it's me. We're done here.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Stay in place and wait?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Grr, you're the boss. Ain't like I got a choice.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Looks like we chose the wrong day to come back.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Why do you say that?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Rain.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: I hate the rain more than anything.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: It's the rainy season. I already told you before we came back.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Now that you don't have your little brother trimming your fur for you, I think you oughta go across the street right now and get it all shaved off.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Watch it, or that mop's gonna come right off your scalp.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: I actually was considering it myself, but my barber talked me out of it. Said my head's lopsided, I'd look ugly.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: But, I gotta hand it to you for findin' a way to make money so quick.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Hmph. Looks like you spent too much time in Lungmen, Capone.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: That Lin fella, sure he's got a few tricks up his sleeve and all, but doesn't Lungmen's governor have him pinned down pretty good?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: But this is Siracusa. And here, the famiglie run the show.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: It's easy to find an odd job or two.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: With so many famiglie running around, everyone always needs some capable hands.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Alright, maybe I was in Lungmen too long, but what really surprises me is how they're still running the same playbook they used to when I left Siracusa.

spans.text: in Lungmen too long, but what really surprises me is how they're still running the same playbook they used to when I left Siracusa.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: The famiglie control everything in this city from the shadows, but they never walk out onto the stage.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Why do you say that?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: A new city is about to be born. On the surface, they're in the middle of voting for its administrator.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: But the truth is, the famiglie backing these people are constantly jockeying for power.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: What the hell are you even talking about? If we didn't lose our own city, we'd be doin' the same exact thing.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: I've been away from Siracusa for a long time, Gambino. Was it eight years? Ten?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: That's a drop in the bucket. What's gonna change in that amount of time?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: It's long enough to change the way I see a lotta things, but clearly not long enough to fix your shortsightedness.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: You know, it ain't like we came to no peace agreement, you and me. Our work just isn't done yet.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: If you're so eager to die, I'm glad to send you on your way.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: How can you be sure that you won't be the one dying?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Hah...

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: How'd you know...?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Bartender, get your ass out here!

steps.name: Bartender
steps.text: I didn't think the two of you were on such good terms.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Haha, looks like your patron ain't as reliable as you thought, Gambino.

steps.name: Bartender
steps.text: Let's be clear here. As long as the two of you complete my commission, I naturally will not mistreat you.

steps.name: Bartender
steps.text: However, the commission is not yet complete.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: You think you can double-cross me?!

steps.name: Bartender
steps.text: Double-cross? If this is your idea of a double-cross, then I recommend you open your eyes a bit wider, Sicilian.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: So, where does that put us now?

steps.name: Bartender
steps.text: I need to see what you two are capable of—right here, right now. It's that simple.

steps.name: Bartender
steps.text: As long as you walk out of this alley alive, you pass.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: I thought you were gonna say you'd take both of us at once.

steps.name: Bartender
steps.text: Haha, my brothers would rake me over the coals for that one. 'You weren't going to let anyone pass in the first place,' or something like that.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: You sure talk a big game.

steps.name: Bartender
steps.text: I'm looking forward to meeting both of you again.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Pretentious bastard. Thinks he's human just because he got used to the city.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Hah... It's been a while since I've heard that.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Looks like we don't have a choice.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: I'll make sure he figures out who doesn't have a choice.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Heh. If I knew I'd be fighting for my life back in Siracusa, I would've just stayed home.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Was that your call to make?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Alright, fine. If we didn't show up, we probably would've been turned into mille-feuille within a day.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: But we followed her here, and she went and disappeared without a word.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: As if she was saying, 'I brought you back home. Now you're free to do whatever you want, go fend for yourselves.'

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: The moment you start thinking that is when she pops up right in front of you. You've jinxed it.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: You look like you got used to life here as well.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: She will come for us.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Lemme ask you this. In Siracusa, who's in bigger danger—a wolf who leaves the pack and goes rogue, or two strays?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Well that's new. Never thought you'd fess up to being a stray mutt.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: I ain't dumb enough to act like I ain't lost everything.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Wish you'd admitted it sooner.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Still, it's pretty obvious that she's tryin' to play with fire right under Signora Sicilia's nose.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Right. We ain't even shit on the side of the road to that woman. And I won't stand for it. If I get the chance, I swear I'm gonna kill her.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: But then there's her. She doesn't even give a damn about Signora Sicilia.

spans.text: She doesn't even give a damn about Signora Sicilia.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: The same Signora Sicilia who sends us a letter and gets us shakin' in our boots.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: And that wasn't enough to get her back to Siracusa. But now, she's back, all over another lone wolf.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Oh, what was it that she asked again? Right, how we ended up so scared of Signora Sicilia?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: You scared of her, Capone?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Honestly, yeah. Nobody can really go against Signora Sicilia.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Every Siracusan's afraid of her.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: So, you wanna see how she dies?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: I wanna see how she lives.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Hate to admit it, but I'm with you.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: That's why we need to stay alive.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Another civil servant got attacked? And a Bellone associate to boot?

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: Yeah, someone's clearly trying to pick a fight.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Hah, serves 'em right. If you ask me, it's probably the Rossatis behind it. Those scumbags and their bag of petty tricks. Disgusting.

steps.name: Skeptical Mafioso
steps.text: But, a lot of the Dodici Famiglie have already said they support the Bellones taking over the new city.

steps.name: Skeptical Mafioso
steps.text: So what's the point of pulling a stunt like this now?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Hmph, hard to say. The Don's son, Leontuzzo, is now a secretary at il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: If someone has the skills to take him out along with il Ministro himself, wouldn't that blow things wide open again?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Considering that runt's dumb enough to set his own famiglia aside to be a yes-man for the government.

steps.name: Skeptical Mafioso
steps.text: You say that, but are you forgetting how many associates ate shit over the last two years because they underestimated him? Oh, I almost forgot, you were one of them.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Bah. I'll admit, the runt's got some talent, but that's only because the don's been sitting on his hands the whole time! Once he decides to call the shots...

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: That's true. The don hasn't said anything yet, and the Bellones can't name themselves the winners so soon.
Enough.
The entire room suddenly falls silent, the clamor and chatter from before seeming like nothing more than an illusion.
I don't care what you believe deep down, but during this tense time, you don't make light of the situation, and you don't do anything rash.
I know what you're all thinking. I get it.
Of the Dodici Famiglie, only our Famiglia Saluzzo hasn't yet placed our wager.
It is still too soon for that.

steps.name: Mafiosi
steps.text: Yes, Don Alberto.
Since time immemorial, Famiglia Saluzzo has always been like this.
One is allowed to think, but not to advise. Because Alberto Saluzzo calls all the shots.
Alberto never allows anyone to question his decisions.
Nobody in the famiglia finds this unusual. They say that the Saluzzos' strength comes from the fact that Alberto is always correct.
Everyone's here? My, now that I look closely, I see a lot of old faces.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: You... You're...
But, that is not to say that there are no rebels. Only, most of them have been erased from the famiglia.
And were never heard from again.
With the exception of a white wolf named Lappland.
She pulls a chair over and props her feet up on the table, as if she owns the place.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Who let her in?

steps.name: Saluzzo Guard
steps.text: Don Alberto, sh-she killed everyone outside and forced her way in...

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: This is a famiglia meeting. Get her out of here.

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: Signorina, I mean, Lappland... The Don has asked you to leave.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I turned down Signora Sicilia's lunch invitation and rushed back like a good little fowlbeast, eager to return to its nest.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: This hideout we have in Volsinii... it's kinda drab, compared to the old Saluzzo stronghold.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Tony, do you really have to treat me so cold?

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: You're no longer an associate of this famiglia.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What, you think I came back to beg the old man to let me back into this damned—I mean, this most distinguished famiglia?

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: Please watch your words, signorina.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Right, right. Even though I was so disgracefully kicked out, this famiglia has always had a special place in my heart.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So, at this critically important time, I have chosen to come back home, at risk to my own life, ignoring my father's disdainful glare, to bring back a vital piece of intelligence.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Does that not move you to tears?

steps.name: Skeptical Mafioso
steps.text: Lappland... Even if you are the Don's own daughter, you've overstepped your bounds.

steps.name: Skeptical Mafioso
steps.text: This is no place for you to run roughshod...

steps.name: Skeptical Mafioso
steps.text: You... Nngh... Urgh...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Never seen that guy before. Was he new?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Y-Yes! S-Signorina Lappland.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You're so cruel, Father, to doubt the sincerity of my actions.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You got my desk dirty, Lappland.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Desks can be replaced, right?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Let's hear it then. Your so-called 'vital intelligence.'

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Texas.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: The same Texas you let go?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: That's right. Bellone brought her back.
Lappland squints at her father.
This homecoming has not inspired a single shred of emotion within her.
She carries with her only a faint glimmer of amusement as to what might happen. Or rather, what she is about to make happen.
Because, she has been in such environments far too many times in her life.
She has returned.
The thoughts that inadvertently bubble up in her mind seem ever so laughable.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Celli——

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Just call me Texas.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Alright, Texas. How does it feel to be back in Siracusa?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Not too great.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I can imagine. If I were you, I wouldn't feel too great about suddenly being forced to go somewhere, even if it was my homeland.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Though, if this isn't too much to ask, I'd like you to imagine this as well: your father suddenly forced a 'bodyguard' onto you, and she's a whole lot stronger than you. That's not a great feeling either.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Understandable.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That's what I wanted to hear.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Unfortunately, I don't have the power to let you leave.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: All I can say is, I hope we can both do what we need to do.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Go ahead and get changed. We had this outfit custom-tailored in old Famiglia Texas style. I hope you can be my bodyguard tonight and accompany me to the banquet.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Sure.
Beside Texas lies the well-pressed suit that Famiglia Bellone has prepared for her.
She looks toward the tightly-shut door.
She knows what she is supposed to do.
To fulfill Zaaro's contract, she needs to exit this room, kill a few irrelevant people, create some chaos, and then finally, kill a few important people.
Irrelevant, or important. This is the attitude Siracusans have toward life.
She, too, used to think like that.
Even now that she has learned to see the world through a different lens, as soon as she stepped back into this city, she quickly realized that these practices were still ever so familiar to her.
She has returned.
The thoughts that inadvertently bubble up in her mind fill her with disgust.
